summary: Re-tested iteration_294 across backend + frontend. Backend contract now passes: /use keeps ITEMS_ROWS placeholder inside tbody. However, frontend renderDocumentTemplate still leaves injected rows commented inside tbody (0 visible rows), so row rendering contract is still broken in UI preview/print/PDF source HTML.

integration_issues.issue: ITEMS_ROWS replacement runs in wrong order: raw token replacement happens before comment token replacement, producing tbody like <!--<tr>...</tr>--> and resulting in 0 rendered rows.

action_items: Frontend: in renderDocumentTemplate, replace comment placeholder first (<!--{{ITEMS_ROWS}}-->) before replacing raw {{ITEMS_ROWS}} to avoid commented <tr> rows.
Re-test DocumentPrint preview tbody row count after fix (should be >=1 when items exist).
Re-verify print/PDF output after row fix to ensure exported/printed table includes visible item rows.
Auth playbook deep checks (bcrypt prefix, httpOnly cookies, brute-force lockout, seed_admin update path) were not fully executed in this scoped retest.
critical_code_review_comments: RCA confirmed from runtime DOM: tbody innerHTML became '<!--<tr>...</tr>-->' which proves replacement order bug in /app/frontend/src/utils/documentTemplate.js.
Backend sanitizer/registry fix is effective now (iter294 backend regression is green: 3/3).

success_rate.frontend: 70% (login/load/template resolve OK; tbody row rendering still failing)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend /use placeholder contract is fixed. Current blocker is frontend replacement order causing commented tbody rows. After frontend fix, re-run DocumentPrint preview + PDF/print regression.
rca of the issue: Repro: open /print, fill item fields, inspect [data-testid='document-resolved-template-sheet'] tbody => 0 tr nodes and tbodyHtml contains commented row markup. Root cause: renderDocumentTemplate replaces '{{ITEMS_ROWS}}' before '<!--{{ITEMS_ROWS}}-->', so comment wrapper remains and rows are inert comments. Mitigation: reorder replacement logic to process comment marker first (or regex-replace both patterns atomically).
